summary: Since 0025502, any parsed mention makes a message 'addressed', and an addressed message is withheld from every follower it does not name. parseMentions still reads ordinary @-tokens as handles: JSDoc tags, decorators, ts directives, version-like tokens and @everyone. A routine code or status message is therefore silently withheld from every follower of its topic. The commit fixed exactly this failure for package scopes and left the rest of the class open.
failure: parseMentions('fixed the JSDoc: added `@param topic` and `@returns`') -> ['param','returns']. routesTo(msg, 'carol', {followed:true, mentionFilter:false}) -> false, so no follower gets the push. Same for 'use @Injectable() here' -> ['Injectable'], '// @ts-expect-error' -> ['ts-expect-error'], '@dataclass' -> ['dataclass'], 'x @1.2.3' -> ['1.2.3'], '@everyone heads up' -> ['everyone']. Reproduced via tsx against src/mentions.ts and src/transport/push-loop.ts routesTo.
remediation: At minimum, have parseMentions skip inline code spans and fenced code blocks (strip `...` and ```...``` before matching), since code is where most non-handle @-tokens live. The routing fix underneath is a transport decision, so surface it: an addressed message should silence other followers only when the mention can name a participant (for example, a handle that resolveIdentity or the operator directory recognises). Otherwise it should degrade to broadcast.

summary: The directory guard grades `${directory} ${INBOUND_TRUST_BOUNDARY}`. The shipped instructions are '... You are <handle>; ... A config can therefore load and then throw from withInboundTrustBoundary at every bridge build or HTTP session. summary: The read-before-you-speak guard treats 'in the SeenSet' as 'handed to the agent'. On-start catch-up warms the SeenSet with the whole backlog it pages over and hands the agent none of it, so after any boot the guard waves a blind post through. Because the guard's read then goes through deliverPage with resumeFrom === stored, it also moves the agent's read position past that backlog. The backlog can then no longer be reached by a since-less parley_fetch_recent, which is the exact loss catchup.ts says it exists to prevent. The same root cause covers messages the push handler marks seen (seen.firstSeen at push-loop.ts:330) but never shows: messages addressed to another handle, everything except mentions under mention_filter, and emits that failed.
failure: Reproduced with a test against buildBridge and FakePlugin (catchup.on_start defaults to true, live_push both true and false). Bob posts 'old1' and 'decided: plan B' to ctx before boot. After boot the agent calls parley_post {topic:'ctx', content:'I propose plan A'} without reading and gets {posted:true}. Expected per DESIGN §7, the README and TOOL_TEXT.post: {posted:false, unread:[old1, decided: plan B]}. A following since-less parley_fetch_recent then returns only ['I propose plan A'], so both backlog messages are unreachable by resume. Every existing guard test in addressing.test.ts posts the peer message after buildBridge, so none of them covers a pre-boot backlog.
remediation: Give the guard its own record of what was actually handed to the agent, separate from the dedup window. Populate it in push-loop route() only after emitChannel resolves, and in deliverPage for parley_fetch_recent pages and for pages the guard itself returns as unread. Catch-up must never write it. The guard's unread is then kept minus handed minus own. Keep the read-position advance in the guard read only for pages whose messages are all handed or returned as unread, which holds once unread is computed from the handed record.

remediationCheck.reliesOn: deliverPage's compare-and-set `if (read.resumeFrom === stored && nextCursor !== stored) readState.set(t, nextCursor)`, and route()'s `await emitChannel(server, m)` resolving only after notification() succeeds.
remediationCheck.newlyRejects: A post right after boot to a topic with a pre-boot backlog the agent never fetched, which is now held with that backlog as unread. Also a post on a topic whose only unread messages were addressed to other handles, which is now held too. Whether that second case is wanted is a product decision the doc does not settle.

remediationCheck.hidesOrFixes: Fixes the boot-time bypass and the position skip. A HANDED_MAX bound on the new record could still evict entries under heavy traffic, which leans toward holding a post, never toward passing a blind one.
remediationCheck.interleavings: A push emit that resolves while a guard read is in flight: the message may be counted unread once and handed by the guard. That costs a duplicate, never a loss.

summary: Every live message waits on opts.own.settled(), which resolves only when the count of in-flight writes drops to 0, on a single queue shared by all topics and the mention feed. One parley_post whose plugin.post never settles (a network hang, a backend that never answers) stops push delivery for the whole bridge. Writes that keep overlapping have the same effect without any single write hanging, because the shared idle promise does not resolve until the count reaches zero. recordPush runs before the queue, so parley_live_status reports 'delivering' while nothing reaches the agent.
failure: Reproduced with a FakePlugin subclass whose post() never resolves for content 'hang', with live_push enabled. The agent calls parley_post {topic:'ctx', content:'hang', force:true}, which never returns. Bob then posts 'urgent' on ctx. After 300 ms the client has received pushes=[] and parley_live_status answers {decided:true, topics:[{topic:'ctx', status:'delivering', pushed:1, reconciled:0}]}. Nothing is delivered for as long as the write hangs, and the health tool reports the opposite.
remediation: Bound the echo wait. Snapshot only the writes in flight when the message arrives, and wait for those or a short deadline (for example a few seconds), whichever comes first. Do not wait for global idleness. Track per-write promises in OwnPosts rather than one idle promise, so that later writes cannot extend the wait.

remediationCheck.reliesOn: OwnPosts.track's `finally { if (--this.inFlight === 0) this.release(); }`. The replacement needs a per-write settle promise, which the code does not have today.
remediationCheck.newlyAccepts: An echo of a write slower than the deadline is pushed back to its author, which is the self-echo the wait exists to prevent, but only for writes slower than the bound.
remediationCheck.testsThatWouldFail: None found. I looked at addressing.test.ts 'nothing an instance wrote is pushed back to it', whose FakePlugin and MentionFeedPlugin echo synchronously inside post(), well within any deadline. The 3 tests that the remove-settled mutation killed also use synchronous echoes.
remediationCheck.hidesOrFixes: Fixes the starvation. The ledger still counts a message as pushed before the gates, so a slow route() can still report 'delivering' ahead of the emit for up to the deadline.
remediationCheck.interleavings: (a) Echo arrives during its own write, and the write returns before the deadline: recognised. (b) Echo arrives during a write that hangs: emitted after the deadline. (c) Two messages queued behind one hung write: both waits use the same snapshot and are released together at the deadline, in order. (d) A new write starts while a message waits: it is not in the snapshot and does not extend the wait.

summary: On a successful exchange, forgetCode() erases every record of the authorization code, and the grant it mints has an unrelated random grantId. summary: A refusal the server returns during a READER's handshake (WRONGPASS after a password rotation, or an ACL user disabled) never reaches serverRefusal(). node-redis reports it as the reconnect strategy's generic 'cannot reach' error, or once the client has been ready, as 'The client is offline'. The real ErrorReply survives only in client.ts's lastEmittedError WeakMap, and only openCommandClient reads that. Two results. (1) A long poll gives up a 2000ms budget in about 2ms with an empty page. Core then naps and opens another doomed reader on every iteration for the whole budget. This is exactly what the blockingRead comment and the README ('fails the call with a labelled error rather than being reported as an empty long poll') promise cannot happen. (2) The subscribe loop's reader reconnects into WRONGPASS forever. It writes 'DEGRADED … The client is offline' and never writes STOPPED, and nothing ever names WRONGPASS, even though WRONGPASS is in PERMANENT_CODES and the README says the DEGRADED line carries 'the server's own error'. The suite cannot see this: subscribe-hardening's 'subscribe/blocking fetchRecent: WRONGPASS … is permanent' rows inject WRONGPASS as an XREAD rejection, and real node-redis never produces that (only AUTH answers WRONGPASS, inside the handshake).
failure: Reproduced on redis:7-alpine. With subscribe(topic), the same rotation, then CLIENT KILL of the reader: after 6s stderr shows only 'parley-redis: live delivery DEGRADED for topic 'rot' — 5 stream reads in a row failed and it is still retrying: The client is offline.' There is no STOPPED line and no WRONGPASS.

Rethrowing `err` would not work: err is the pluginError 'cannot reach', which labelled passes through untouched, so the refusal text is lost. In runReadLoop, on a non-refusal xRead error, check `serverRefusal(lastEmittedError.get(reader))`. If it is defined, take the STOPPED branch (retire, then reportLiveDeliveryStopped, which already applies fromServer). Otherwise pass its text into the DEGRADED line.

summary: post() and ensureRoom/resolveOrCreateRoom capture no generation. http() reads this.token and this.baseUrl live and takes its generation at call time. So a post issued while connected to homeserver A, still resolving its room when a bare connect() moves the plugin to B, carries on against B with B's token: it joins or creates there and writes the message on B. The read path (existingRoom) gates on generation; the write path does not. This breaks the package's own invariant 'no seam call reaches the homeserver without the credential of its own generation'.
failure: Reproduced with the fake (test/zz/reconnect-post.test.ts): post(t,'written under gen A') on synapse.fake, with connect({homeserver_url: other.fake}) landing during the /directory lookup. The trace is `other.fake .../rooms/!room0:fake/join Bearer tok-other.fake`, then `/state`, then `PUT .../send` on other.fake, and post resolves `$e0:fake`. A room id resolved on A is joined on B. With aliasExists=false, POST /createRoom runs on B. In a subscribe, ensureRoom has the same side effects on B before its stale gate returns. Separately, ensureRoom's .catch deletes the cell for its key even when a newer generation has refilled it, defeating the memo's single-create promise.
remediation: Make the generation a caller-supplied argument. post() captures `const generation = this.generation` before ensureRoom; ensureRoom/resolveOrCreateRoom/adoptRoom/lookupAlias pass it to http(), which throws `[parley-matrix] ... superseded` when this.generation !== generation, instead of capturing its own. In ensureRoom's catch, delete only when `this.rooms.get(key) === pending`.

Core's new read-before-you-speak guard (tools.ts unreadBeforePost) runs that same fetchRecent before every post, so during a probe outage the guard passes and the post is written over messages the author never read. The post's own join then enters the room anyway.

summary: post() never checks which stream acked the publish. Say the topic's own stream is removed out-of-band and another stream now captures its subject. That message sits in FOREIGN, not in the topic's stream. fetchRecent then throws 'does not exist, but FOREIGN... already captures', and the subscribe loop retries streams.add against the overlap every second without ever recovering. summary: A record append that fails part-way leaves its bytes in the file. tornTail only adds a newline before the next write, so the fragment survives as a mid-file garbage line. The next load counts it as damage (`dropped = true` → lost) and mints a fresh epoch. That invalidates every cursor every agent holds, over a record that was never handed out. A failure after a complete line is the opposite problem: post has rejected with 'did not record it … unreachable here', but the record is on disk and served after restart. A caller that retried has double-posted.

In the variant where the whole line was written before the throw: post rejects ('did not record it'), and after restart contentsOf returns ['subject','after']. Both reproduced.
remediation: In StoreFile.write, read fstatSync(fd).size before appendFileSync. In the catch, ftruncateSync(fd, size) so the file returns to its pre-write bytes, and clear tornTail. summary: Redaction only knows the request URL (redactUrls(text, url)). Credentials that travel in init.headers (Authorization: Bearer/Bot/Basic, used by Matrix, Discord, Zulip, Slack) are never redacted from the error body or the transport message. Both feed `<label> → …` errors, which become isError tool results, i.e. model context.
failure: (a) A server that answers 401 with `bad auth: ${req.headers.authorization}` yields `L → 401: bad auth: Bearer s3cr3tTOKENvalue123`. (b) A token with an embedded control character, e.g. 'Bearer s3cr3tTOKEN\nvalue123' from a folded YAML scalar, makes undici throw before any network I/O, and fetchWithRetry rejects with `L → transport: Headers.append: "Bearer s3cr3tTOKEN value123" is an invalid header value.`, the full credential. Both reproduced with a vitest probe.
remediation: Extend the redaction input from `url` to `{ url, headers }`. Collect the values of credential-carrying headers (authorization, proxy-authorization, cookie, x-api-key, plus whatever the caller marks), split each on whitespace and control characters into pieces longer than ~8 characters, and strike every piece. Undici rewrites the newline to a space, so the raw value alone will not match. Apply it in errorBody and in fetchOnce's transport branch.

summary: The close handler sets `this.wsReady = undefined` before its `if (!helloSeen) return`, and gates only on `this.ws !== ws`. After a handshake timeout or an error, the failed socket A stays as this.ws until the next attempt B's openSocket finishes its apps.connections.open round trip and assigns `this.ws = wsB`. If A's close event lands in that window, A clears B's in-flight wsReady, and a concurrent ensureSocket caller dials a second socket alongside B. The extra socket is held in `sockets` and closed only at stop(). It costs one of the roughly 10 connections per app token, and its later close is ignored (this.ws !== ws).
failure: Not reproduced; traced. The window is close latency (up to ws's 30 s close timeout against an edge that never answers a close frame) falling inside B's HTTP round trip. It is narrow, and needs a second concurrent ensureSocket caller.
remediation: Move `this.wsReady = undefined` below the `if (!helloSeen) return` gate. A pre-hello failure's wsReady is already cleared by ensureSocket's attempt.catch. Or clear `this.ws` when the handshake settles with an error.

remediationCheck.reliesOn: ensureSocket attempt.catch: `if (this.wsReady === attempt) this.wsReady = undefined;`, which already owns clearing a failed attempt.
remediationCheck.testsThatWouldFail: untested. connection-lifecycle 'pre-hello-close' rows rely on the attempt rejection clearing wsReady, which the remediation keeps.
remediationCheck.hidesOrFixes: Fixes the clobber. The orphaned-socket accounting is otherwise unchanged.

summary: The mark() JSDoc relies on 'write it AFTER the line it names', so that a crash leaves the .hw BELOW the file. That holds for a process crash, but neither the appended line nor the .hw is fsynced, and the kernel gives no writeback order across two files on power loss. A .hw that reaches disk ahead of its record makes the next load see `marked > issued` and re-mint the epoch, refusing every held cursor.
